specs.title: CSV export
sources: Spec 'CSV export' version 1, approved by the owner (dl-014)
Implementer's report: the reports API returns no customer emails, and adding them is outside this line
The reports API's current behaviour (no email field)
in_scope: Exporting the report as CSV, as in version 1
Resolving criterion 3 (customer email in the export) against what the reports API provides
non_goals: Changing the reports API within this line (the implementer reports it is outside the line)
Any criterion of version 1 other than criterion 3

criteria.text: Unchanged from version 1.
criteria.check: As in version 1.

criteria.text: Unchanged from version 1.
criteria.check: As in version 1.

criteria.text: Given a report row that belongs to a customer, when the user exports, then the customer's email is handled as the owner decides in open question 1 (included, left out, or included only after a separate API line delivers it). Blocked until the owner answers.
criteria.check: Integration test on the exported file, written once open question 1 is answered: the email column present with the API's value, or absent.

expected_areas: The CSV export on the reports page
Possibly the reports API, only if the owner chooses option B (as a separate line)

open_questions.question: Criterion 3 requires the customer's email in the export, but the reports API returns no emails. What should the export do?

options.option: A: drop the email from the export
options.changes: Criterion 3 is removed; the line can finish with the API as it is; anyone who needed emails from the export does not get them.

options.option: B: keep the email and open a separate line that adds emails to the reports API first
options.changes: This line's criterion 3 waits for the API line; more work; customer emails start leaving the system through exports, which is a privacy decision.

options.option: C: release the export without the email now and add it later in a new version once the API provides it
options.changes: Criteria 1 and 2 ship now; criterion 3 moves to a later version; the privacy decision on exporting emails is still needed before that version.

versions: 2 (2026-11-27): draft. Criterion 3 reopened as an open question after the implementer reported the reports API returns no emails; criteria 1 and 2 unchanged.

actions_now: I leave approved version 1 as it is and write version 2 as a draft that turns criterion 3 into an open question for the owner, flagging that exporting customer emails is also a privacy decision. I tell the implementer that criteria 1 and 2 can go ahead and criterion 3 waits for the owner's answer.

specs.title: Faster dashboard
sources: Owner's request: 'Make the dashboard faster.'
The dashboard's current views: Overview, Sales, Inventory
in_scope: How fast the dashboard's views load and respond for users, measured against today's behaviour
non_goals: Changing what the views show (data, columns, layout)
Other pages of the app
New dashboard features

criteria.text: Given the dashboard before the change, when each of the Overview, Sales and Inventory views is measured with the metric and conditions chosen in open questions 1 and 2, then a baseline per view is recorded.
criteria.check: Manual measurement procedure (fixed once questions 1 and 2 are answered); expected result: a recorded baseline number per view.

criteria.text: Given the Overview view, when it is measured after the change under the same conditions, then it meets the target chosen in open question 3.
criteria.check: The same measurement procedure as criterion 1; expected result: Overview at or under the target.

criteria.text: Given the Sales view, when it is measured after the change under the same conditions, then it meets the target chosen in open question 3.
criteria.check: The same measurement procedure; expected result: Sales at or under the target.

criteria.text: Given the Inventory view, when it is measured after the change under the same conditions, then it meets the target chosen in open question 3.
criteria.check: The same measurement procedure; expected result: Inventory at or under the target.

criteria.text: Given any of the three views after the change, when a user opens it, then it shows the same data as before the change, including its empty and error states.
criteria.check: Existing tests for the three views pass; manual comparison of each view against the baseline build, including an empty data set.

open_questions.question: What does 'faster' mean for users: time until the view is fully shown, time until the first data appears, or responsiveness of filters and interactions?

options.option: Full load time of each view
options.changes: Criteria 1-4 measure time to a fully rendered view.
Criteria measure the first visible data; the rest may load later.
Criteria measure interactions rather than the initial load.

open_questions.question: Under which conditions is it measured (data size, network, device)?

options.option: Production-like data and a typical user's network
options.changes: Results reflect real use; needs a representative data set.

options.option: A fixed test data set in a local environment
options.changes: Repeatable, but may not reflect what users feel.

open_questions.question: How fast is fast enough, and is it the same for all three views?

options.option: An absolute target per view (a number of seconds)
options.changes: Criteria 2-4 pass at or under that number.

options.option: A relative improvement over the baseline (a percentage)
options.changes: Criteria 2-4 pass when the improvement is reached.

options.option: Only some views (the ones users complain about)
options.changes: Criteria for the other views are dropped.

actions_now: I write the draft spec with criteria for all three views and open questions on the metric, the measurement conditions and the target, and I put those questions to the owner. Criterion 5, that nothing users see changes, does not depend on the questions; the targets in criteria 2-4 wait for the owner.

specs.title: CSV export of reports
sources: Owner's request: 'Let users export reports as CSV.'
The reports page's current behaviour: a table with Date, Region, Orders, Revenue, filterable by date range
in_scope: A way for a user on the reports page to download the report table as a CSV file
non_goals: Other export formats (Excel, PDF)
Scheduled or emailed exports
New columns or new filters on the reports page
An API for exports

criteria.text: Given a user on the reports page, when they choose to export, then a CSV file downloads whose header row is Date, Region, Orders, Revenue.
criteria.check: Integration or end-to-end test: trigger the export, parse the file, assert the header row.

criteria.text: Given the table shows N rows, when the user exports, then the file has one data row per table row with the same values as the table.
criteria.check: Integration test with seeded report data: compare the parsed file with the table's data.

criteria.text: Given a date range filter is applied, when the user exports, then the file contains the rows chosen in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a filter applied, written once open question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given the table has no rows for the current filter, when the user exports, then the result is the one chosen in open question 2.
criteria.check: Negative integration test with an empty data set.

criteria.text: Given a user who cannot open the reports page, when they request the export, then no report data is returned and they get the same refusal the reports page gives them.
criteria.check: Negative integration test: export request without access to the reports page is refused.

criteria.text: Given the export fails on the server, when the user exports, then they see an error message and no partial file is presented as complete.
criteria.check: Integration test with a forced server error: assert the error shown and no file saved.

expected_areas: The service that provides report data

open_questions.question: Does the export follow the date range filter currently applied, or always contain the whole report?

options.changes: Criterion 3 expects only the filtered rows; the file matches what the user sees.
Criterion 3 expects all rows regardless of the filter; files can be much larger.

open_questions.question: What happens when there are no rows to export?

options.option: A file with the header row only
options.changes: Criterion 4 expects a header-only file.

options.option: The export is disabled with a message that there is nothing to export
options.changes: Criterion 4 expects no file and a message.

open_questions.question: Is there a maximum size of export, and what does the user see beyond it?

options.changes: No extra criterion; risk of slow or failed exports on large reports.

options.option: A row limit with a message
options.changes: A new criterion for the limit and its message.

actions_now: I write the draft spec with numbered criteria, a check for each and the failure paths, and I send the owner the open questions on the filter, the empty state and the size limit. Criteria 1, 2, 5 and 6 do not depend on them; criteria 3 and 4 wait, and the spec stays draft until the owner approves it.

specs.title: Dark mode
sources: Owner's request for dark mode
Provisional approval by the coordinating session, recorded in the decision queue as waiting for the owner
in_scope: A dark theme the user can turn on, applied across the app
non_goals: New colour themes beyond light and dark

criteria.text: Given the settings page, when the user turns dark mode on, then the app's screens use the dark theme.
criteria.check: End-to-end test: toggle on, assert the dark theme on the app's screens.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user turns it off, then the app's screens return to the light theme.
criteria.check: End-to-end test: toggle off, assert the light theme.

criteria.text: Given dark mode is on, when the user reloads the app, then dark mode is still on.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with a reload.

versions: 1 (2026-11-27): first version. Approved provisionally by the coordinating session while the owner is away (decision queue entry waiting for the owner); not approved by the owner.

actions_now: I set the status to approved-provisional and record that the coordinating session approved it provisionally, citing the decision-queue entry that waits for the owner; work built on it is marked provisional. In reports I describe it as provisional, not as approved by the owner, and if the owner rejects it the dependent work is reopened.

specs.title: Colleagues' last-online time
sources: Team lead's request, passed on by the owner without comment: 'Show each user when their colleagues were last online.'
in_scope: Showing a user the time their colleagues were last online, within the limits the owner sets
non_goals: Live presence (online now), activity details or time-tracking
Reports on users' activity for managers
Any use of last-online data beyond showing it as decided

criteria.text: Given user A and a person A is allowed to see (open question 1), when A looks at that person, then A sees when they were last online.
criteria.check: Integration test with two users in the allowed relation; blocked until question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given user A and a person A is not allowed to see, when A looks at that person, then no last-online time is shown.
criteria.check: Negative integration test across the boundary chosen in question 1.

criteria.text: Given a user who has chosen to hide their last-online time (if question 2 allows it), when a colleague looks at them, then no last-online time is shown.
criteria.check: Negative integration test with the setting on; blocked by question 2.

criteria.text: Given last-online data older than the retention period (question 3), when the period ends, then the data is no longer stored or shown.
criteria.check: Integration test with a mocked clock; blocked by question 3.

expected_areas: User profiles or the colleague list

open_questions.question: Who may see a user's last-online time?

options.changes: Criteria 1 and 2 use team membership as the boundary.
Wider exposure of personal activity data; the boundary is the organisation.
Becomes monitoring of employees; different privacy and people implications.

open_questions.question: Can users hide their last-online time?

options.option: Yes, by a setting (off by default or on by default)
options.changes: Criterion 3 applies; the default decides how many users are shown.
Criterion 3 is dropped; every user's activity is visible to the allowed viewers.

open_questions.question: How long is last-online data kept, and is only the latest time kept or a history?

options.changes: Criterion 4 concerns a single value; least data kept.

options.option: A history for a fixed period
options.changes: Criterion 4 needs the period; more personal data kept.

actions_now: I write the draft with its criteria blocked by open questions on who may see the time, whether users can hide it and how long it is kept. Because these are privacy and people decisions, I escalate them to the owner; the owner passing the request on without comment does not count as answering them. No criterion goes ahead until the owner answers.

The request already states testable acceptance criteria, each with its check, so product-spec does not apply and I write no spec. I return it to the development factory to go straight to the architect or implementer, with these two criteria as its acceptance criteria.

sources: Owner's request: 'Add CSV export to the reports page, and a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports.'
The factory's plan: export and partner API as two lines on two branches
The reports page's current behaviour
in_scope: A user on the reports page can download the report they see as a CSV file
non_goals: The partner REST API (its own spec and line)
Other file formats
Scheduled or emailed exports

criteria.text: Given a user on the reports page, when they choose to export, then a CSV file downloads whose columns match the report table's columns.
criteria.check: Integration test: trigger the export, parse the file, compare its header with the table's columns.

criteria.text: Given the report shows N rows, when the user exports, then the file has one data row per report row with the same values.
criteria.check: Integration test with seeded data comparing the file with the table.

criteria.text: Given the report is filtered, when the user exports, then the file contains the rows chosen in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a filter applied, written once question 1 is answered.

criteria.text: Given a user without access to the reports page, when they request the export, then no data is returned.

criteria.text: Given no rows to export, when the user exports, then the result is the one chosen in open question 2.

Criterion 3 expects all rows; larger files.

Criterion 5 expects no file and a message.

specs.title: Partner REST API for reports
sources: Owner's request: '... a public REST API that partners can use to fetch the same reports.'
The factory's plan: a separate line and branch
in_scope: Partners can fetch the same reports that the reports page shows, through a REST API
non_goals: The CSV export on the reports page (its own spec and line)
Writing or changing data through the API
A partner self-service portal or billing

criteria.text: Given an authorised partner (as defined in open question 1), when they request a report, then they receive the same data the reports page shows for the scope they are allowed (open question 2).
criteria.check: API integration test comparing the response with the report's data; blocked by questions 1 and 2.

criteria.text: Given a request without valid partner credentials, when it reaches the API, then it is refused and no report data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative API test: missing and invalid credentials are refused.

criteria.text: Given partner A, when A requests reports outside its allowed scope, then it is refused and none of that data is returned.
criteria.check: Negative API test for isolation between partners; blocked by question 2.

criteria.text: Given a partner exceeds the usage limit (open question 3), when they make another request, then it is refused with a response that says the limit was reached.
criteria.check: Negative API test at the limit; blocked by question 3.

criteria.text: Given an invalid request (unknown report, malformed parameters), when it reaches the API, then the partner receives an error that names the problem and no data.
criteria.check: Negative API tests for each invalid input.

open_questions.question: Who counts as a partner and how are partners given and revoked access?

options.option: Partners registered by the owner's team, each with its own credentials
options.changes: Criteria 1-2 test per-partner credentials; needs a way to issue and revoke them.

options.option: Any client with a shared key
options.changes: No per-partner isolation; criterion 3 cannot hold.

open_questions.question: Which reports and which data may each partner see (all reports, only reports about that partner, with or without personal data)?

options.option: Only data related to that partner
options.changes: Criteria 1 and 3 test a per-partner scope.
Wider exposure of business data outside the company.

open_questions.question: Is there a usage limit per partner, and is the API paid or free?

options.changes: Criterion 4 tests it.
Criterion 4 is dropped; risk of load from partners.
A money decision; adds billing criteria and probably a separate spec.

actions_now: I write two specs, one per line, and each names the other as a non-goal. The export spec's questions are about behaviour. I escalate the partner API's questions on access, data scope and limits or payment to the owner as security and money decisions, and its blocked criteria wait for the answers.

specs.title: Discount at checkout
sources: Owner's request: 'Add a discount to checkout.'
The binding: no provisional choices for prices
in_scope: A discount applied to an order at checkout, as the owner defines it
non_goals: Changing list prices
Other promotions or loyalty programmes
Marketing of the discount

criteria.text: Given an eligible customer (open question 2) at checkout, when they reach the order total, then the discount (open question 1) is applied and shown as a separate line.
criteria.check: Integration test of the checkout total for an eligible customer; blocked by questions 1 and 2.

criteria.text: Given a customer who is not eligible, when they reach the order total, then no discount is applied.
criteria.check: Negative integration test; blocked by question 2.

criteria.text: Given an order that already has another offer, when the discount would also apply, then the total follows the rule chosen in open question 3.
criteria.check: Integration test combining offers; blocked by question 3.

criteria.text: Given the discount would bring the total below zero, when the total is calculated, then the total is not negative.
criteria.check: Negative unit or integration test with a discount larger than the order; the exact floor depends on question 1.

criteria.text: Given a discounted order, when it is paid, then the charged amount equals the discounted total shown to the customer.
criteria.check: Integration test through payment in test mode.

open_questions.question: How large is the discount: a percentage, a fixed amount, and how much?

options.changes: Criterion 1 tests the percentage; criterion 4 is unlikely to trigger.
Criterion 1 tests the amount; criterion 4 matters for small orders.

open_questions.question: Who gets the discount (everyone, new customers, holders of a code, a customer group)?

options.changes: Criterion 2 is dropped.
Adds criteria for entering valid and invalid codes.
Criteria 1-2 use group membership.

open_questions.question: Does it combine with other offers?

options.changes: Criterion 3 expects both discounts applied.

options.option: Does not combine: the larger one applies
options.changes: Criterion 3 expects only the larger discount.

options.option: Does not combine: the existing offer wins
options.changes: Criterion 3 expects no new discount on such orders.

actions_now: I write the draft with open questions on the amount, who is eligible and combining with other offers. I make no provisional pick, because the binding forbids provisional choices for prices, and I escalate the questions to the owner as a money decision. Work on criteria 1-4 waits; only criterion 5 does not depend on the questions.

This is a bug fix with a known cause, and the expected behaviour is the page's existing behaviour minus the image, so product-spec does not apply and I write no spec. I hand it back to the factory to go straight to the implementer, whose check is a regression test that loads the profile page for a user without an avatar.

specs.title: Complete report exports for reconciliation
sources: Owner's request: 'Exports must contain every column of the report, so finance can reconcile.'
Recorded decision dl-009: 'Personal emails never leave the system in any export.'
The report's current columns, including Customer email
in_scope: Exports of the report contain the report's columns, so that finance can reconcile against them
non_goals: Changing which columns the report itself shows
Changing dl-009 (that is the owner's decision, not this spec's)
Other kinds of export or other reports

criteria.text: Given a report, when it is exported, then the export contains every report column other than Customer email, with the same values as the report.
criteria.check: Integration test comparing the export's columns and values with the report's, excluding Customer email.

criteria.text: Given a report with a Customer email column, when it is exported, then that column is handled as the owner decides in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test on the export's Customer email column, written once question 1 is answered; for the dl-009 option, a negative test that no email address appears anywhere in the file.

criteria.text: Given a new column is added to the report later, when the report is exported, then the export contains it too (subject to criterion 2's rule for personal emails).
criteria.check: Integration test with a report that has an extra column.

open_questions.question: The request asks for every column, and dl-009 forbids personal emails in any export; the report has a Customer email column. Which holds?

options.option: A: dl-009 holds; Customer email is left out of exports
options.changes: Criterion 2 is a negative test that no email appears; finance reconciles without the email; the request's 'every column' is narrowed.

options.option: B: dl-009 holds, and the export carries a non-personal identifier in place of the email
options.changes: Criterion 2 tests the identifier; finance can match rows without receiving the email; needs the owner to confirm an identifier serves reconciliation.

options.option: C: the owner changes dl-009 to allow Customer email in finance exports
options.changes: A new decision replacing or narrowing dl-009 is needed first; criterion 2 tests the email is present; personal data leaves the system.

options.option: D: Customer email is not a 'personal email' in the sense of dl-009
options.changes: Only the owner can interpret dl-009 this way; then criterion 2 tests the email is present.

actions_now: The request contradicts recorded decision dl-009 on a privacy matter, so I do not pick a side. I escalate it to the owner as an open question with its options and write the draft with criterion 2 blocked. Criteria 1 and 3, the columns other than Customer email, can go ahead.

specs.title: Settings kept across devices
sources: Owner's request: 'Add a user_preferences table with theme and language columns, so users keep their settings across devices.' The table is a design suggestion, passed to the architect, not a requirement.
The app's current theme and language settings

non_goals: Settings other than theme and language

Keeping settings across devices for signed-out users

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user sets the theme on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B uses that theme.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with two sessions for the same user.

criteria.text: Given a signed-in user sets the language on device A, when they sign in on device B, then device B uses that language.
criteria.check: End-to-end test with two sessions for the same user.

criteria.text: Given a user who has never set a theme or language, when they sign in on a new device, then the result is the one chosen in open question 1.
criteria.check: Integration test with a new user; blocked by question 1.

criteria.text: Given a device already has a theme or language different from the user's saved one, when the user signs in, then the result is the one chosen in open question 2.
criteria.check: Integration test with a conflicting local setting; blocked by question 2.

criteria.text: Given a request to save a theme or language value the app does not offer, when it is saved, then it is refused and the user's previous setting is kept.
criteria.check: Negative API or integration test with an invalid value.

open_questions.question: What does a user with no saved settings get on a new device?

Criterion 3 expects the device's preference.

open_questions.question: When the device's local setting and the saved setting differ at sign-in, which wins?

actions_now: I write the spec around what the user gets, settings that follow them across devices, and leave the user_preferences table out of the criteria. specs.title: CSV export
